title: What is the Webflow Cloud?
summary: Webflow Cloud is not just a faster hosting or a minor infrastructure update. It is a complete reimagining of what you can build in Webflow.
body_text: TL;DR: Webflow Cloud is a serverless hosting platform that lets you deploy full-stack web applications (built with Next.js or Astro) directly alongside your Webflow site. It eliminates the need for separate hosting, enables programmatic SEO at scale, and brings developers, designers, and marketers together on one unified platform. Sites run on Cloudflare's global edge network with automatic scaling, 99.99% uptime, and built-in storage options. All images sourced from Memberstack’s YouTube video on the Webflow Cloud by Julian Galluzzo. What is the Webflow Cloud: Overview If you have ever built a website in Webflow, you probably loved the visual design tools. The drag-and-drop interface, the polished animations, and the ability to create beautiful sites without writing code. But if you tried pushing the platform beyond basic marketing sites, you likely encountered limitations. Webflow Cloud changes all of that. Launched in May 2025, Webflow Cloud represents a platform evolution. It is not just a faster hosting or a minor infrastructure update. It is a complete reimagining of what you can build in Webflow. Webflow Cloud enables developers to deploy web applications using frameworks like Next.js and Astro directly within their Webflow sites. This means your marketing site, your web application, your custom tools, and your dynamic content can all live under one domain, managed through one platform, without fragmented customer experiences or disconnected workflows. Key Features of Webflow Cloud Full-Stack Application Hosting Webflow Cloud supports Next.js and Astro frameworks. Deploy server-side rendered applications and complete web experiences that integrate with your Webflow-designed pages. The platform connects to GitHub for automated deployments when you push code changes. Global Edge Hosting and Unlimited Scaling Webflow Cloud uses Cloudflare's network to deliver content from data centers worldwide. Visitors get faster load times regardless of location. Bandwidth caps are removed. Sites scale automatically from 1,000 to 1 million visitors without capacity planning. This helps during traffic spikes from product launches or viral content. Dynamic Rendering with Cloudflare Workers Cloudflare Workers serve dynamic content from the edge. Build features that change based on location, time, user authentication, or other variables without performance penalties. This allows you to personalize landing pages, location-specific content, A/B testing, and real-time data displays. DevLink Integration DevLink exports Webflow components into React code. Buttons, navigation menus, forms, and layouts created in Webflow become reusable React components. Designers work in the visual environment, developers import designs as code. Cloud Storage Options Webflow Cloud provides three types of serverless storage, all deployed automatically with your application, SQLite, Key-Value Store, and Object Storage. You can mix and match these storage types based on your specific data requirements. All three are scoped to your Webflow Cloud with no vendor lock-in required. Framework Support and Future Roadmap Currently, Webflow Cloud supports Next.js and Astro within JavaScript and React. However, the goal is to be able to work over a variety of platforms in time. This means broader support for additional frameworks and libraries is planned, allowing developers to use the tools that best fit their workflows without sacrificing performance or visual control. Why It Matters: SEO, Speed, and Growth SEO & Speed Performance Google's ranking algorithm heavily weighs page speed and Core Web Vitals. Webflow Cloud's edge hosting architecture significantly improves these metrics by reducing server response times and delivering content from geographically distributed locations. Faster load times translate directly to better search rankings. Lower bounce rates result from improved user experience. Higher engagement metrics signal quality to search engines. All of these factors compound to boost your organic search visibility. Beyond speed, Webflow Cloud enables SEO at scale. You can generate thousands of landing pages dynamically from structured data without manual page creation. Think location-based pages for every city you serve, product detail pages for extensive catalogs, or long-tail keyword landing pages that would be impractical to build individually. Growth and Scalability Automatic scaling grows with your business. Launch marketing campaigns or run promotions without infrastructure concerns. Build more sophisticated experiences as you evolve: marketing sites, customer portals, internal tools, or headless ecommerce on the same platform. Real-World Use Cases Uses For Full-Stack Applications: Build advanced functionality without leaving Webflow: Booking engines : Custom reservation systems with availability checking, authentication, and payment processing Pricing calculators : Interactive tools pulling real-time API data with personalized quotes Headless ecommerce : Custom shopping experiences integrated with existing platforms SaaS onboarding : Multi-step signup flows with personalized dashboards AI integrations : Chatbots, content generation tools, and personalized recommendations Uses For Programmatic SEO: Generate thousands of pages automatically from structured data. Connect your product catalog, location database, or keyword research to deploy server-rendered, indexable pages: Location pages : Automatic generation for every city, region, or service area Long-tail campaigns : Thousands of pages targeting specific keyword variations Dynamic PPC pages : Personalized landing pages adapting to ad parameters ABM pages : Customized content for target accounts All pages live on your main domain, maintaining unified brand experience and domain authority. Uses For Internal Tools: Build custom internal systems that integrate with your site infrastructure: Employee directories : Searchable staff databases with profiles and hierarchies Content dashboards : Custom interfaces for moderation and approval workflows Analytics portals : Reporting tools with tailored visualizations Lead management : CRM-style interfaces for prospect tracking and sales coordination Real Company Example: TurboHome TurboHome, a real estate technology company, uses Webflow Cloud to deliver a personalized home-buying experience. They integrate over 200,000 MLS (Multiple Listing Service) listings through a Next.js application hosted seamlessly with their Webflow marketing site. As Rob Baldwin, CTO of TurboHome, explains in the May 2025 press release on Webflow Cloud: "Our engineering and marketing teams now work from the same system, saving time, eliminating complexity, and ensuring brand consistency across every touchpoint." This best illustrates the core value of Webflow Cloud: bringing together technical and non-technical teams on a unified platform that serves both application requirements and beautiful, on-brand marketing experiences. Security and Compliance Webflow Cloud provides enterprise-grade security: SOC 2 Type II Certification : Independent security verification GDPR-Ready Infrastructure : European privacy regulation compliance tools Audit Logs and APIs : Comprehensive tracking for compliance reporting 99.99% Uptime SLA : Reliable infrastructure SSL/TLS Encryption : Automatic HTTPS with modern encryption DDoS Protection : Built-in protection through Cloudflare This security foundation means your sites can pass legal and IT security reviews without extensive additional configuration or third-party security tools. It positions Webflow Cloud as an advanced solution without top-tier pricing for most use cases. How to Get Started and Migration Possibilities Starting Fresh with Webflow Cloud Setup takes approximately 30 minutes: Install the Webflow CLI using npm Create a new Webflow site by cloning a starter template Initialize your app using the CLI to create a Next.js or Astro application Connect to GitHub for version control and automated deployments Create a Webflow Cloud project by linking your GitHub repository Deploy by pushing your code The Webflow CLI handles much of the complexity, generating project scaffolding and connecting your development environment to Webflow's infrastructure. Migrating Existing Sites If you have an existing Webflow site, migration is straightforward. Your current site continues functioning while you add new application features. Webflow even provides a Migration Playbook for developers, agencies, and teams moving larger projects, covering edge cases, performance optimization, and best practices. Development Workflow Once set up, the workflow becomes streamlined. Designers work in Webflow's visual editor creating components and layouts. Developers import those components and build in their code editor. Content teams manage pages through Webflow's CMS interface. Deployment happens automatically when code is pushed to GitHub. Everyone works within their area of expertise using familiar tools while the platform handles integration. Webflow Cloud Cost Official Release and Pricing Webflow Cloud was officially released out of beta in July 2025 and is now available to all users. The platform implements a transparent usage-based pricing model. All paid Webflow site plans include Webflow Cloud access, with usage limits varying by plan tier. The pricing model is based on three metrics: Bandwidth : Total data transferred between your application and visitors, pooled with overall site bandwidth. Requests : Number of application requests handled monthly, including page loads, server-side executions, and API calls. CPU Time : Total compute time used to process logic and run server-side code, measured in milliseconds. Surge Pricing Protection All paid site plans include complimentary surge protection to prevent unexpected overages from traffic spikes. If you exceed your monthly allocation once, you receive notifications but face no charges. If you exceed limits again in the following month, your plan automatically upgrades at the start of your next billing cycle based on the lower usage from those two months. Plan Considerations Starter and Basic site plans have limitations: you can only mount to webflow.io domains (not custom domains), and a Webflow badge remains on your site. Higher-tier plans (CMS, Business, Enterprise) remove these restrictions and offer higher usage limits. For most professional applications, you will want at least a CMS or Business site plan. Webflow Cloud Support Documentation and Learning Resources Webflow provides extensive resources for learning and troubleshooting Webflow Cloud: Developer Documentation : Technical guides covering setup, configuration, and best practices Webflow University : Video tutorials and courses Getting Started Guides : Step-by-step walkthroughs Migration Playbooks : Documentation for moving existing sites Customer Support and Community Webflow also offers customer support via email with a 48-hour response time target. Enterprise customers receive enhanced support with faster response times and dedicated account management. The Webflow community also provides valuable assistance through an active Community Forum where users help other users solve problems, a searchable Help Center knowledge base, and a network of over 1,500 Certified Webflow Partners offering professional services and technical expertise. Conclusion Webflow Cloud bridges the gap between visual design tools and full-stack development capabilities, creating a place where designers, developers, and marketers collaborate effectively without fragmented tools or disconnected workflows. Whether you are a freelancer landing bigger projects, an agency migrating client sites, a startup needing modern infrastructure without a DevOps team, or an enterprise requiring scalable secure hosting with visual editing capabilities, Webflow Cloud offers a compelling solution. To learn more about Webflow Cloud, visit webflow.com/cloud . Frequently Asked Questions What is the difference between Webflow hosting and Webflow Cloud? Traditional Webflow hosting serves static sites and CMS-driven content with excellent performance for marketing websites and blogs. Webflow Cloud extends these capabilities by enabling full-stack applications with server-side logic, real-time data processing, complex integrations, and dynamic content generation that goes beyond static hosting limitations. Which frameworks does Webflow Cloud support? Currently, Webflow Cloud supports the JavaScript and React ecosystem, specifically Next.js and Astro frameworks. The platform's roadmap includes expanding with broader support for additional frameworks and libraries planned for future releases. Can I use Webflow Cloud with my existing Webflow site? Yes. You can add Webflow Cloud capabilities to existing Webflow sites. Your current pages continue functioning normally while you add features. Do I need coding knowledge to use Webflow Cloud? Non-technical team members do not need coding knowledge to work on the visual site components, though there are instances in which some prior knowledge may help. How does DevLink work? DevLink exports Webflow components as React code that you can import into your Webflow Cloud applications. This ensures visual elements maintain consistency and creates a unified design. What happens if I exceed my usage limits? All paid plans include surge protection. Your first overage in a billing month generates notifications but no charges, giving you time to assess usage. If you exceed limits in a second consecutive month, your plan automatically upgrades at the start of your next billing cycle based on your lower usage from those two months. Is Webflow Cloud suitable for enterprise applications? Yes. Webflow Cloud includes SOC 2 Type II certification, GDPR-ready infrastructure, audit logs, 99.99% uptime SLA, and other security features. These capabilities make it suitable for businesses with compliance requirements and high reliability needs. How do I get access to Webflow Cloud? Webflow Cloud is currently available on all paid Webflow site plans.

title: Reporte de la Industria Automotriz en México 2024
summary: Análisis detallado de la industria automotriz en México en 2024: tendencias de ventas, financiamiento, transición hacia autos eléctricos, y el impacto socioeconómico en los consumidores.
body_text: Tabla de Contenido Introducción 1. Ventas de Vehículos Nuevos 2. Autofinanciamiento 3. Postventa y Servicios 4. Tendencias en Arrendamiento 5. Vehículos Híbridos y Eléctricos Conclusiones ¿Quieres un seguro de auto que sí te cuide de verdad? Todo en línea. Reclamos más rápidos. Servicio inmejorable. Introducción En 2024, la industria automotriz mexicana continúa siendo un pilar esencial de la economía. A pesar de un entorno socioeconómico desafiante, caracterizado por la moderación de la inflación y un crecimiento económico lento, el mercado automotriz ha demostrado resiliencia. El incremento en ventas de vehículos nuevos, la expansión en servicios postventa y el uso de alternativas de financiamiento refuerzan la confianza de los consumidores, quienes, en gran medida, se han inclinado por opciones de financiamiento diversificadas. Este reporte explora el panorama de la industria en México, analizando ventas, postventa, financiamiento y arrendamiento. 1. Ventas de Vehículos Nuevos En el periodo de enero a octubre de 2024, la venta de vehículos ligeros alcanzó 1,201,464 unidades, un incremento del 10.2% comparado con 2023 ( INEGI ). Las preferencias de los consumidores reflejan una marcada inclinación hacia marcas que combinan tecnología, eficiencia de combustible y precios competitivos. Nissan, Chevrolet y Volkswagen continúan como líderes, mientras que Mazda y KIA han aumentado su participación en más del 20% anual ( AMDA ), capturando consumidores jóvenes y familias que buscan vehículos de buena relación calidad-precio. Cabe destacar la increíble subida que han tenido las marcas chinas, que, combinadas, ahora cuentan con un 9,2% del mercado, representando un crecimiento del 20% respecto a 2023 ( AMDA ). Este crecimiento es significativo en un contexto en el que los precios de los vehículos se han elevado debido al incremento en los costos logísticos, y puede atribuirse a diversos factores. En primer lugar, en los últimos años, el índice de envejecimiento está al alza ( INEGI ), lo que significa que una parte considerable de la población ha alcanzado la edad para conducir. Esto tiene un gran impacto considerando que en 2020 la edad media de la población era de 29 años, y que la edad media de compra de vehículos nuevos es de 37 años ( Autocosmos ). Aunque no haya datos más allá del 2020, si el crecimiento en la edad media ha continuado con la tendencia de los 10 años previos al 2020 (+2 años por año), podemos deducir que en 2024 una gran parte de la población ha entrado en la edad de compra de vehículos nuevos. Le sigue que la estabilización económica tras los impactos de la pandemia y la reducción en las tasas de inflación, que subió dramáticamente en 2021 y 2022 ( Gobierno de México ), han generado mayor confianza en los consumidores, incentivando la adquisición de bienes duraderos como los automóviles respecto a los años anteriores. Adicionalmente, la gradual bajada en tasas de interés respecto a 2022 y 2023 ( Banco Central ) han hecho más accesibles los créditos automotrices, impulsando las ventas en este segmento. Otro elemento clave ha sido la recuperación de inventarios en las concesionarias, luego de la crisis global de semiconductores que afectó la producción de vehículos en años anteriores. Finalmente, los programas de incentivos gubernamentales en coches eléctricos, como la deducción fiscal en la importación, exención de varios impuestos (tenencia, verificación e ISAN) y exenciones en las inversiones en baterías, así como el aumento de promociones por parte de las marcas, han jugado un papel importante en motivar la compra de de este tipo de automóviles, tanto nuevos como seminuevos. En términos geográficos, la Ciudad de México y el Estado de México lideran el mercado automotriz en el país, con 186,107 y 126,665 unidades vendidas respectivamente durante los primeros nueve meses de 2024. Esto refleja el peso económico de estas entidades, que concentran una proporción significativa del Producto Interno Bruto nacional, así como la alta densidad de población y la alta tasa de urbanización. 2. Autofinanciamiento El financiamiento continúa siendo un pilar clave para la adquisición de vehículos nuevos en México, representando el 60% de las ventas totales entre enero y septiembre de 2024. Este esquema resulta esencial en un contexto en el cual, como se ha comentado anteriormente, los precios van al alza, especialmente en segmentos como compactos y subcompactos, donde los consumidores buscan opciones más accesibles. Además, dado que una gran parte del incremento en las ventas proviene de un segmento joven (que entra en la edad media de compra de vehículos nuevos), es lógico pensar que un gran porcentaje de ellos no ha podido permitirse la compra pagando por adelantado. Entidades como la Ciudad de México, Estado de México y Nuevo León lideran en colocaciones, en línea con el mayor volumen de ventas de vehículos ligeros que hay en esos estados, como se comentó anteriormente. En cuanto a las opciones de financiamiento, los programas de autofinanciamiento de marca, como SICREA de Nissan y ConAuto de Ford, han logrado capturar el 73% del mercado, superando a los bancos comerciales. Este dominio se debe a la capacidad de estas empresas de ofrecer plazos más flexibles y tasas de interés competitivas, lo que refuerza la preferencia de los consumidores por esquemas que les brindan mayor estabilidad financiera ( AMIS ). Por otra parte, los plazos más frecuentes en los financiamientos se han mantenido entre 36 y 48 meses, facilitando la accesibilidad para un mayor número de compradores. Además, el financiamiento para vehículos de lujo experimentó un aumento significativo de 9.3 puntos porcentuales, reflejando el crecimiento de este segmento a pesar de los desafíos económicos del país. Este panorama evidencia cómo el financiamiento continúa adaptándose a las necesidades de los consumidores, permitiendo que el mercado automotriz mantenga su dinamismo y competitividad. 3. Postventa y Servicios A pesar del crecimiento en 2024 en la venta de automóviles, el parque vehicular en México sigue envejeciendo. Esto se debe a varios factores. En primer lugar, el aumento en los precios de los vehículos nuevos provocado por la inflación (que aunque haya bajado sigue siendo alta), así como el incremento en los costes de producción, hacen que un gran segmento de la población opte por la opción más económica, esta siendo los vehículos de segunda mano. Por otro lado, a pesar de la percepción del consumidor y según varios reportes de JD Power y Consumer Reports, la vida media de los coches ha aumentado con el avance de los años. Por ejemplo, en 1980 la vida media de un vehículo particular era de 8-10 años, cuando actualmente es de 13 años en México ( INEGI ). Esto se debe a la mejora en materiales y diseño, así como los avances en tecnología, especialmente en los motores, sistemas de transmisión, frenos y suspensión. Este incremento en la vida media, unido a la mejora y facilidad en la que se reciben los servicios de mantenimiento, hace que la demanda por dichos servicios de mantenimiento y postventa vaya en aumento. Los servicios de mantenimiento preventivo lideran la demanda en talleres automotrices, representando el 45.1% de las órdenes, reflejo de la prioridad de los conductores por evitar problemas mayores, y los servicios correctivos ocupan el 27.6%, atendiendo fallas en unidades más antiguas. El ticket promedio de reparación aumentó un 2.9% respecto al año anterior, influido por la dependencia en la importación de piezas y un incremento en la demanda de estos servicios. 4. Tendencias en Arrendamiento En el primer semestre de 2024, las empresas especializadas en arrendamiento adquirieron 26,648 unidades de vehículos ligeros, representando un segmento relevante del mercado automotriz. Aunque esta modalidad mostró una leve disminución del 3.8% en comparación con el año anterior, sigue siendo una opción atractiva, especialmente en un entorno donde las empresas y usuarios buscan flexibilidad financiera y operativa ( AMAVe ). El arrendamiento se ha consolidado como una solución ideal para quienes necesitan vehículos sin asumir la responsabilidad de propiedad a largo plazo. Este modelo permite a las empresas optimizar sus flotas, acceder a modelos más recientes y reducir gastos relacionados con mantenimiento y depreciación. Además, para usuarios particulares, representa una alternativa práctica frente a la compra tradicional, ya que elimina compromisos como enganches elevados o financiamiento a largo plazo. A pesar del leve retroceso anual, el arrendamiento sigue desempeñando un papel crucial en el impulso en la tenencia de vehículos ligeros en el país. 5. Vehículos Híbridos y Eléctricos El segmento de vehículos híbridos y eléctricos ha experimentado un crecimiento notable en 2024, con unas ventas entre Enero y Julio de 65,232 unidades, lo que representa un incremento del 80% respecto al mismo periodo del año 2023. Este avance refleja un interés creciente en la movilidad sustentable, impulsado por una mayor conciencia ambiental, avances tecnológicos y un cambio gradual en las preferencias de los consumidores. Sin embargo, aunque prometedor, su participación en el mercado total sigue siendo baja, lo que evidencia que el cambio hacia la electrificación del transporte se enfrenta aún a desafíos. Una encuesta realizada por Momento con más de 100 participantes reveló que el 67% de los conductores está considerando, o al menos evaluando, la posibilidad de cambiar a un coche eléctrico en los próximos cinco años. La razón principal para este cambio es la preocupación por el medio ambiente, seguida del ahorro en combustible que los vehículos eléctricos ofrecen en comparación con sus equivalentes de combustión interna. Estos resultados refuerzan una tendencia clara: el conductor mexicano muestra un interés cada vez mayor en opciones de movilidad sostenible, motivado por los beneficios ecológicos y económicos. Sin embargo, aún existen barreras significativas que limitan una adopción más ágil de los vehículos eléctricos. Según la misma encuesta, los precios elevados de estos autos representan uno de los mayores obstáculos para los consumidores. Aunque los costos de baterías han disminuido con el tiempo, los modelos eléctricos todavía son significativamente más caros que los vehículos tradicionales, lo que limita su accesibilidad, especialmente para la clase media. Otra preocupación importante es la infraestructura de carga. Muchos conductores consideran que cargar un coche eléctrico es inconveniente debido a la limitada disponibilidad de estaciones de carga pública y los largos tiempos necesarios para recargar completamente las baterías. Además, en áreas fuera de las grandes ciudades, esta infraestructura es aún más escasa, lo que genera incertidumbre sobre la viabilidad de utilizar estos vehículos en trayectos largos o en regiones menos urbanizadas. Conclusiones La industria automotriz en México en 2024 muestra un crecimiento constante en ventas de vehículos nuevos, y una mayor consolidación de servicios postventa y financiamiento. En un entorno de moderada recuperación económica, los consumidores están optando por alternativas de financiamiento, a pesar de las elevadas tasas de interés, así como por el mantenimiento de sus vehículos existentes a través de servicios postventa. La tendencia hacia la movilidad sustentable también está presente, aunque todavía en sus primeras etapas. Las oportunidades para el sector automotriz en México incluyen la optimización de programas de financiamiento, así como el fortalecimiento de la postventa para captar un segmento creciente de consumidores que buscan prolongar la vida útil de sus vehículos.

title: Toyota Financial Services Expands Headquarters
summary: FRISCO, Texas (July 15, 2026) – Toyota Financial Services (TFS) this week began occupying a newly constructed 242,000-square-foot, seven-story building at its headquarters campus, capable of seating over 1,000 team members. This extension of the Toyota North America campus called […]
body_text: FRISCO, Texas (July 15, 2026) – Toyota Financial Services (TFS) this week began occupying a newly constructed 242,000-square-foot, seven-story building at its headquarters campus, capable of seating over 1,000 team members. This extension of the Toyota North America campus called “TFS North”, adds much-needed office space, additional parking, and facilitates the ability to co-locate larger teams. TFS team members supporting customer experience, dealer experience and data & technology will work out of this location. TFS North exemplifies thoughtful appreciation for team member well-being and productivity throughout the building. Recognized as one of the largest mass timber office spaces in the United States, the building’s commitment to health and sustainability is more than just a feature. The extensive use of Southern Yellow Pine timber creates a warm and inviting atmosphere. Tim Conlon, real estate senior manager, shared that one of the most exciting priorities in the design of TFS North was creating a space that feels open, welcoming, and connected. “The natural wood structure was intentionally highlighted, and wide-open views were preserved throughout the office to bring warmth and character into the workplace.” The overall result increases visibility, communication, and collaboration, helping team members feel more connected to one another and to the environment around them. Team members will enjoy a host of amenities, including a state-of-the-art gym and locker rooms, micro markets, furnished balconies, and a future restaurant. More subtle features include white noise systems that help reduce distractions and enhance concentration in open areas, window shades that adjust with the sun’s movement, and daylight harvesting that adjusts lighting to save energy. An adjoining 800-space parking structure makes for easy parking and EV charging. Plus, soon-to-be-installed space counters will make it easy for team members to find a parking spot. Alec Hagey, president and CEO of TFS, highlighted the advantages of the expanded office space, saying, “Our new building provides a modern environment where team members can come together to collaborate and provide the best possible service to our customers and dealers. As team members occupy this building, we will be able to reconfigure our existing headquarters space to reduce overcrowding, enhance collaboration, and foster innovation to position our company for future growth.” Additional TFS teams will continue to move into the space in the coming weeks with full occupancy anticipated in the fall of 2026. Related Media Related Images Share on Facebook Share on Linkedin Send email Copy Link About Toyota Financial Services Toyota Financial Services (TFS) is the brand for finance and related products for Toyota in the United States, offering retail auto financing and leasing through Toyota Motor Credit Corporation (TMCC) and Toyota Lease Trust. TFS also offers vehicle and payment protection products through Toyota Motor Insurance Services (TMIS). The company services Lexus dealers and customers using the Lexus Financial Services brand. As of March 31, 2026, TFS employed approximately 3,900 team members nationwide and had over $150 billion in assets. The company is part of a worldwide network of comprehensive financial services offered by Toyota Financial Services Corporation, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Toyota Motor Corporation. We announce material financial information using the investor relations section of our website ( www.toyotafinancial.com ) and SEC filings. We use these channels, press releases, and social media to communicate about our company, our services and other issues. While not all information we post on social media is of a material nature, some information could be material. Therefore, we encourage those interested in our company to review our posts on Facebook at www.facebook.com/toyotafinancial and Instagram at https://www.instagram.com/toyotafinancial/ . title: Refinity Partners with Zeton to Build a Repeatable Modular Plastic-to-Olefins Plant
summary: Refinity, an Innventure company, taps Zeton to design and build a 10 kta modular plant converting mixed plastic waste directly into circular olefins—a repeatable model for global deployment.
body_text: Partnership pairs Refinity's conversion technology with Zeton's modular fabrication expertise to accelerate the path from demonstration to commercialization ORLANDO, Fla., July 23rd, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Refinity, an Innventure, Inc. (NASDAQ: INV) company transforming hard-to-recycle plastic waste into valuable chemical intermediates, today announced it has selected Zeton Inc. to complete final detailed engineering plans for, and to build and deliver, a 10,000 tonne-per-annum (10 kta) modular waste plastics-to-olefins commercial demonstration plant. Zeton is a global specialist in the design and fabrication of modular pilot, demonstration, and production plants. This is an important step to advance Refinity's commercialization strategy of circular olefin production sited alongside third party petrochemical steam crackers, with Refinity to supply circular feedstock to the $300B ethylene and propylene markets, as well as the $400B polyethylene and polypropylene plastics markets. Zeton's modular, factory-built approach is expected to provide Refinity with a repeatable plant design required to scale the business. Refinity plans to site the 10 kta plant alongside a third-party petrochemical steam cracker to demonstrate circular olefin production at commercial conditions. The plant will run Refinity's fluidized bed conversion technology, which converts mixed plastic waste into light olefin gas streams, primarily ethylene and propylene, which will be fed directly into post-steam cracker operations. We believe this will be a first-of-a-kind commercial plant demonstrating direct conversion of mixed plastic waste to light olefins. Compared to processes that produce pyrolysis oil for use in steam cracking, we believe that our integrated approach will enable a two- to three-fold increase in yield from plastic waste to olefin products. In a second element of the collaboration, Zeton is contracted to build a unit designed to integrate with an existing fluidized bed system, supporting Refinity's scale-up capability for converting light gas products into jet-fuel-range liquids. This work is expected to advance a pathway central to Refinity's sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) strategy and complement the catalytic upgrading capabilities Refinity recently licensed from Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL). "Scaling a technology like ours is as much about execution as it is about chemistry," said Bill Grieco, CEO of Refinity. "We have deep collaborations with Dow, VTT, Pacific Northwest National Lab, and others. Working with Zeton is a natural next step as we believe Zeton's experience delivering modular process systems will help mitigate our scale-up risks and accelerate delivery of the 10 kta plant. Just as important, we anticipate replicating Zeton’s construction model in connection with our global commercialization strategy." Refinity anticipates completing initial production runs and validating practical operating costs as the modular systems are delivered and integrated. The engagement of Zeton is expected to help Refinity achieve its goal of creating a plant design that can be replicated globally at facilities located adjacent to steam cracker sites. About Refinity Refinity, an Innventure (NASDAQ: INV) company, converts difficult-to-recycle mixed plastic waste into drop-in raw materials for the petrochemical industry. Its proprietary DuoZone™ reactor platform targets the roughly 91% of plastic waste* that traditional mechanical recycling cannot handle, producing circular ethylene and propylene along with distillate liquids for sustainable aviation fuel and specialty markets. Refinity holds exclusive global licenses to breakthrough technologies and collaborates with trusted, well-respected partners across the petrochemical industry and leading research institutions. For more information, visit refinity.com. *Reference: United Nations Environment Programme, 2022.
